question: Do iOS signing configuration and release metadata have competing authorities?
verified_evidence: projects.yaml enables openclaw-fork with safe relative outputDir .architecture-reviews.
The last 30 ledger entries contain no failed or timeout run with a continuable checkpoint; openclaw-fork was last reviewed 2026-08-03.
apps/ios/project.yml assigns apps/ios/Signing.xcconfig to five target groups and apps/ios/Config/Signing.xcconfig to two target groups.

The two tracked signing files disagree on signing mode (Manual vs Automatic), team-variable model, provisioning defaults, and available bundle/profile keys while both advertise shared/default signing ownership.

Release metadata has a root authority and generated sync/check tooling: scripts/sync-plugin-versions.ts reads package.json.version, and release-preflight checks plugin, schema, channel metadata, docs and SDK artifacts. Platform version files remain separate intentional consumers checked by dedicated commands; no concrete harmful divergence was observed.
current_conclusion: Verified finding: iOS signing defaults are split across two independently mutable config authorities selected per target. Release version multiplicity was rejected as a finding because explicit generators/checkers establish ownership and no drift was demonstrated.
next_trace: If resumed, inspect git provenance around e60c5105607 and project target requirements to design a single base signing config plus narrowly named release-only override, proving watch/share entitlements do not require the current authority split.
